newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds rose on rising political hopes.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds rose on rising political hopes.

text.p: Argentine bonds rose sharply Monday on the back of rising optimism that the government's economic policies will get the necessary backing from the ruling Peronist Party.
"The market is stronger. Our feeling is that there is a bit more optimism," said the chief trader at a large Argentine bank.
The 5.5 percent dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 rose $0.50 to 115.50 while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 4 due 2002 rose $1 to 96.00.
Traders emphasized though that there was virtually no trade because of the U.S. Labor Day holiday.
The announcement by President Carlos Menem over the weekend about the introduction of labor market reforms was seen in a positive light.
"Labor market reforms are good for expectations because the idea is that structural reforms are continuing," said Agustin Etchebarne, the chief economist at private consultancy C&E Consultores.

In addition, the meeting of the ruling Peronist Party on Thursday called by Menem some weeks ago could represent a serious wathershed for market senitment if Menem is able to persuade his party of the merits of the government's economic policies.
That could go a long way in ridding the market of the uncertainty that has dogged it in recent weeks and lift sentiment that the latest economic measures will soon be passed by Congress.
In the money markets, one day call money rates rose to 8.50 percent from 7.80 percent.
